title: Whether faith is a discursive assent; and whether the Papists use a circular discourse in establishing faith
pass_a_gloss: Article XVI. Whether faith is a discursive assent; and whether the Papists use a circular discourse in establishing faith. 1. Assent is commonly divided into simple (noetic) and dianoetic or discursive. Simple assent is that by which the intellect assents to propositions clear and manifest by their own light. Discursive is that by which it assents to a conclusion because of premises. 2. Divine faith is discursive assent: we assent to the articles of faith because of this middle — God has spoken, or Scripture testifies. It is not simple noetic assent, because the mysteries of faith are not known of themselves by nature's light. 3. The Papists in establishing faith use a circular discourse: they prove Scripture to be God's word from the Church's testimony; they prove the Church infallible from Scripture. This circle is vicious and tends to destroy divine faith. 4. The Orthodox deny the circle: faith's principle is God's own word authenticating itself by intrinsic marks and the Holy Spirit's internal testimony — not the Roman Church's authority as first foundation.
pass_b_english: Article XVI. Whether faith is a discursive assent; and whether the Papists use a circular discourse in establishing faith.
1. Assent is simple (noetic) — to propositions clear by their own light — or discursive (dianoetic) — to a conclusion because of premises.
2. Divine faith is discursive: we assent to the articles because God has spoken, or Scripture testifies. It is not simple noetic assent; faith's mysteries are not self-evident to nature's light.
3. Papists establish faith by a vicious circle: Scripture is God's word because the Church says so; the Church is infallible because Scripture says so. That tends to destroy divine faith.
4. Orthodox deny the circle. Faith's principle is God's word authenticating itself by intrinsic marks and the Spirit's internal testimony — not Rome's authority as first foundation.
source_text:
ART. XVI.
An fides sit assensus discursivus? Et an Pontificii utantur circulari discursu in stabilienda fide.

1. Assensus dividi solet in simplicem (noeticum) & dianoeticum seu discursivum. Simplex assensus est, quo intellectus assentitur propositionibus sua luce claris & manifestis. Discursivus, quo assentitur conclusioni propter praemissas.

2. Fides divina est assensus discursivus: assentimur articulis fidei propter hoc medium — DEUS dixit, seu Scriptura testatur. Non est assensus simplex noeticus, quia mysteria fidei non sunt per se nota lumine naturae.

3. Pontificii in stabilienda fide utuntur discursu circulari: Scripturam esse DEI verbum probant ex Ecclesiae testimonio; Ecclesiam esse infallibilem probant ex Scriptura. Hic circulus vitiosus est, & fidem divinam destruere tendit.

4. Orthodoxi negant circulum: principium fidei est ipsum DEI verbum seipsum authenticans per notas intrinsecas & testimonium Spiritus Sancti internum — non Ecclesiae Romanае authoritas tanquam fundamentum primum.
